# SDK LLM Reference

This file is for AI coding agents integrating the full `@cloak.dev/sdk` surface in external applications.
It is intentionally dense, code-first, and grounded in real exports. Every signature and recipe below maps to
a function or class that actually exists in `@cloak.dev/sdk`.

Use this file as your primary SDK briefing and only fall back to the friendlier `.mdx` guides for conceptual context:

- `/sdk/quickstart`
- `/sdk/request-authentication`
- `/sdk/core-concepts`
- `/sdk/utxo-transactions`
- `/sdk/wallet-integration`
- `/sdk/api-reference`
- `/sdk/error-handling`
- `/sdk/kit-integration`

---

## 1. Package

- Name: `@cloak.dev/sdk`
- Version: `0.2.0`
- Runtime: Node `>=18` and modern browsers. ESM and CJS both shipped (`dist/index.js`, `dist/index.cjs`).
- Types: `dist/index.d.ts`
- Program ID (default, mainnet): `zh1eLd6rSphLejbFfJEneUwzHRfMKxgzrgkfwA6qRkW`
- Devnet program ID: `Zc1kHfp4rajSMeASFDwFFgkHRjv7dFQuLheJoQus27h` (served by the local-only `@cloak.dev/sdk-devnet` fork, see `/development/devnet`; NOT available through the published `@cloak.dev/sdk` NPM package).
- Circuits: the 0.2.0 bundle base is pinned into this SDK build (`DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_URL`), so standard integrations configure nothing. Override with `setCircuitsPath()` or `CLOAK_CIRCUITS_PATH`.
- Submission endpoint: NOT defaulted, by design, so a local or test run can never silently reach production. Pass `relayUrl` in `TransactOptions` on every flow. The SDK reads no environment variable for it; `CLOAK_RELAY_URL` is a convention used by the SDK's own examples and scripts, which read it themselves and pass the value as `relayUrl`. Omitting `relayUrl`, or passing `relayUrl: ""`, makes `transact` / `transfer` / `partialWithdraw` / `fullWithdraw` / `swapUtxo` / `swapWithChange` AND deposits (`externalAmount > 0n`) all throw the same error, before any network call: `Viewing key registration is mandatory: relayUrl is required.` There is no silent fallback to self-submission on the default path, for any flow. The endpoint-pinning bullet below also describes `""` as the caller-signed direct-submission signal; both statements are true and this is the condition that reconciles them: `""` carries that meaning ONLY when `enforceViewingKeyRegistration: false` is passed in the same `TransactOptions`. The viewing-key gate defaults ON and runs first, so on default options `""` never reaches the code that would read it as a signal. Turning the gate off to reach direct submission is unsafe for sends, withdrawals and swaps; see invariant 7. (`swapUtxo` also contains a `relayUrl is required for swapUtxo` throw, but it sits far past the check above and is unreachable unless registration enforcement is turned off; see invariant 7.)
- Endpoint pinning: `relayUrl` no longer SELECTS the endpoint. The allowed origins are fixed when this SDK is built (`RELAY_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST` in `src/config/relay.ts`). Only two values pass the pin: an origin on that allowlist (say `CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL` rather than typing a host), or `""` for caller-signed direct submission. Anything else throws, naming the value and the allowlist. Passing the pin is not the same as reaching submission: `""` only ever behaves as the direct-submission signal when `enforceViewingKeyRegistration: false` is set in the same `TransactOptions`, because the viewing-key gate runs earlier and, on default options, throws `Viewing key registration is mandatory: relayUrl is required.` for every flow including deposits. So an allowlisted origin is the only value a standard integration passes; see invariant 7 before considering the other one. It is not an environment variable because an env var resolves in the consumer process, which is exactly what the pin constrains. To develop against a local stack, REPLACE (never append) the allowlist entry and rebuild.
- RPC is NOT pinned. The caller builds the `Connection`; the SDK never inspects, replaces or proxies it, and ANY non-loopback RPC is fine. A production build refuses only a LOOPBACK RPC (`localhost` / `127.0.0.1`), through `BUILD_ALLOWS_LOCAL_ENDPOINTS`, which is derived from the same allowlist. Never state or imply that an integrator must use a Cloak-operated RPC; that is false.
- Authenticated sender: every relay-submitted flow (private send, withdraw, swap) signs its request body with the END USER'S OWN wallet. Deposits do not, being wallet-signed straight to chain. See invariant 13, §5.8 and `/sdk/request-authentication`.
- Hashing: BN254 Poseidon (via `@lightprotocol/hasher.rs`) + BLAKE3.
- Proof system: Groth16 via `snarkjs`.
- Native companion types: `@solana/web3.js` for `Connection`, `Keypair`, `Transaction`, `PublicKey`. `@solana/kit` is supported for reads (see §4d).

Install:

```bash
npm install @cloak.dev/sdk @solana/web3.js
# Optional:
npm install @solana/spl-token @solana/kit
```

---

## 2. Runtime contract (invariants an agent MUST preserve)

1. UTXO external amount semantics:
   - `externalAmount > 0n` -> **deposit** (SDK submits the transaction directly, signed by the user).
   - `externalAmount < 0n` -> **withdraw / swap** (user does not sign on-chain; SDK handles submission).
   - `externalAmount === 0n` -> **shield-to-shield transfer** (SDK handles submission).
2. Every UTXO transaction has exactly 2 inputs and 2 outputs. The SDK pads for you using `createZeroUtxo()`.
3. UTXO balance identity the circuit enforces:
   `inputSum + externalAmount === outputSum`.
4. Amounts in UTXO flows are ALWAYS `bigint`. Never cast to `number` inside transaction logic.
5. Public inputs for the transact/withdraw-swap proofs are 264-byte payloads; do not hand-pack them.
6. On-chain fee model (read by the program from each pool's `pool_config` PDA and collected by the program into the treasury; `transact` reads the live config before building a fee-bearing proof):
   - SOL: `5_000_000` lamports fixed (`0.005 SOL`) + `0.3 %` variable. SDK helpers: `calculateFee(number)`, `calculateFeeBigint(bigint)`, `isWithdrawAmountSufficient(bigint)`, `getDistributableAmount(number)`.
   - SPL (USDC/USDT, 6 decimals): `450_000` base units fixed (`0.45` token) + `0.3 %` variable, charged in the withdrawn token. The SDK does not compute SPL fees; there is no SPL fee helper.
   - Fees only apply on withdrawal/swap paths. Deposits and shield-to-shield transfers pay zero protocol fee.
   - Minimum deposit: `10_000_000` lamports for SOL, `1_000_000` base units for USDC/USDT.
7. Viewing-key registration is required before scanner/compliance flows can decrypt chain notes. `enforceViewingKeyRegistration: false` in `TransactOptions` is the only thing that turns that check off, and it defaults to enabled. It is also the flag that gates `relayUrl: ""`: with the check on (the default) an empty or omitted `relayUrl` throws before any network call, and only with the check off does `""` act as the caller-signed direct-submission signal described in §1. Do NOT combine it with an omitted or empty `relayUrl`: with the check off and a signer present (`depositorKeypair`, or `signTransaction` + `depositorPublicKey`), `transact` / `transfer` / `partialWithdraw` / `fullWithdraw` submit directly, signed and paid by the user's own key, which links the transaction to that key and loses the privacy the flow exists for. With the check off, no relay and no signer, the call does not fail cleanly either: it reports the problem through `onProgress` and then throws a misleading `commitment indices missing: [-1, -1]` error. Deposits are the one flow where direct submission is correct: they always submit under the depositor's key by design, and require `depositorKeypair` or `signTransaction` + `depositorPublicKey`.
8. Merkle root freshness: treat `RootNotFound` / stale-root errors as retryable. SDK transaction paths already retry these by default; use `preflightCheck` / `waitForRoot` only for advanced/operator flows.
9. Never log secrets: spend keys, viewing keys (`nk`), UTXO private keys, blindings, signed messages, note payloads.
10. Standard integrations should use SDK defaults for program and circuits. Only override for custom/operator deployments. There is no submission-endpoint default: `relayUrl` is required on every flow, and for a standard integration the value is always an allowlisted origin. The other value the pin accepts, `""`, is inert unless invariant 7's check is turned off, and turning it off is not a recipe for a send, withdrawal or swap.
11. In low-level UTXO calls, keep `programId` fixed to `CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID` in one place and do not expose it as user configuration.
12. Minimal scripts should use `KEYPAIR_PATH` + `<lamports>` input; do not use raw secret env vars or float amount parsing.
13. Relay-submitted flows require an authenticated sender, checked BEFORE any proof work:
   - Browser: pass `signMessage` AND `walletPublicKey` (or `depositorPublicKey`) in `TransactOptions`. A wallet adapter cannot supply `depositorKeypair`; never generate browser code that asks for one.
   - Node/server: pass `depositorKeypair`.
   - Neither, or only half of the wallet pair: `transact` / `transfer` / `partialWithdraw` / `fullWithdraw` / `swapUtxo` / `swapWithChange` throw `Cloak <flow> requires an authenticated sender ...` before proof generation. Deposits (`externalAmount > 0n`) are exempt.
   - The authenticated `sender` IS the key screened for sanctions and the key a viewing key is registered against. It MUST be the end user's real wallet, never an ephemeral, session or service-held key. Passing a `depositorKeypair` and a different `walletPublicKey` throws.
   - A private send or withdrawal signs EXACTLY ONCE regardless of network retries. Only `swapUtxo` / `swapWithChange` re-prompt, capped by `maxWalletApprovals` (default 5, floored at 1).
   - Signed requests are valid for `REQUEST_AUTH_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (300); the SDK holds back 15 seconds for transit, so the usable approval budget is 285 seconds. A machine clock more than `REQUEST_AUTH_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECONDS` (30) ahead cannot authenticate at all. Map rejections through `explainRelayAuthRejection`.

---

## 3. Core defaults, constants, and types

```ts
import {
  CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID,           // PublicKey, mainnet + devnet
  NATIVE_SOL_MINT,            // PublicKey, So111...112
  DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_URL, // ".../cloak-circuits/circuits/0.2.0" (ceremony bundle)
  TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_VERSION,     // "0.2.0"
  resolveCircuitsBase,              // explicit arg → CLOAK_CIRCUITS_PATH / CLOAK_CIRCUITS env → pinned default
  MERKLE_TREE_HEIGHT,         // 32
  FIXED_FEE_LAMPORTS,         // 5_000_000
  MIN_DEPOSIT_LAMPORTS,       // 10_000_000
  VARIABLE_FEE_NUMERATOR,     // 3
  VARIABLE_FEE_DENOMINATOR,   // 1000
  VARIABLE_FEE_RATE,          // 0.003
  LAMPORTS_PER_SOL,           // 1_000_000_000
  SIGN_IN_MESSAGE,            // wallet-based viewing-key derivation message
  VERSION,                    // SDK version string
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";
```

Core note/transaction types (from `core/types`):

```ts
type Network = "localnet" | "devnet" | "mainnet" | "testnet";

interface WalletAdapter {
  publicKey: PublicKey | null;
  signTransaction?<T extends Transaction>(tx: T): Promise<T>;
  signAllTransactions?<T extends Transaction>(txs: T[]): Promise<T[]>;
  sendTransaction?(tx: Transaction, connection: Connection, options?: SendOptions): Promise<string>;
}

class CloakError extends Error {
  category: "network" | "indexer" | "prover" | "relay" | "validation" | "wallet" | "environment" | "service";
  retryable: boolean;
  originalError?: Error;
}
```

## 4. Initialization patterns

### 4a. Node.js with a Keypair (server / script)

```ts
import { CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID, CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL, setDebugMode } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";
import { Connection, Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { readFileSync } from "fs";

const signer = Keypair.fromSecretKey(
  Uint8Array.from(JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.env.KEYPAIR_PATH!, "utf8"))),
);

const connection = new Connection(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!, "confirmed");
setDebugMode(true);

// There is no client object. The signer travels per call, in TransactOptions.
const options = {
  connection,
  programId: CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID,
  relayUrl: CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL,
  depositorKeypair: signer,
  walletPublicKey: signer.publicKey,
};
```

### 4b. Browser with `@solana/wallet-adapter`

```ts
import {
  CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID,
  CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL,
  LocalStorageAdapter,
  getPublicKey,
  validateWalletConnected,
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";
import { useWallet } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-react";

const wallet = useWallet();
validateWalletConnected(wallet);

// Persist notes and key material through an explicit storage boundary.
const storage = new LocalStorageAdapter();

const options = {
  connection,
  programId: CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID,
  relayUrl: CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL,
  signTransaction: wallet.signTransaction!, // signs the DEPOSIT transaction
  signMessage: wallet.signMessage!, // authenticates send/withdraw/swap requests + viewing-key registration
  depositorPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
  walletPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
};
```

### 4c. UTXO transaction API (primary runtime entry point)

```ts
import {
  transact,
  partialWithdraw,
  fullWithdraw,
  swapWithChange,
  CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID,
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";
import { Connection } from "@solana/web3.js";

const connection = new Connection(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!, "confirmed");
const programId = CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID;
```

### 4d. Kit-flavored reads alongside SDK

```ts
import { createSolanaRpc, address } from "@solana/kit";
import { Connection } from "@solana/web3.js";

const kitRpc = createSolanaRpc(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!);
const connection = new Connection(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!, "confirmed");

// Reads via Kit:
const balance = await kitRpc.getBalance(address(signer.publicKey.toBase58())).send();
// Writes via SDK (still uses web3.js Connection):
```

For an end-to-end Kit-flavored integration shape, combine the read/write split in this section with the transaction recipes in section 6.

---

## 5. Full capability map

Group exports by responsibility. Every symbol below is a real named export of `@cloak.dev/sdk`.

### 5.1 Package constants and entry points

There is no client class. The transaction entry points are free functions, listed in §5.3.

- `CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID`: `PublicKey`, mainnet program
- `NATIVE_SOL_MINT`: `PublicKey`, SOL pool mint identity
- `VERSION`: string, `"0.2.0"`
- `setDebugMode(enabled: boolean)`: global SDK logging switch
- `LocalStorageAdapter` / `MemoryStorageAdapter`: `StorageAdapter` implementations (see §5.13)

### 5.2 UTXO primitives (primary data model)

```ts
interface UtxoKeypair {
  privateKey: bigint;   // ~252-bit field element
  publicKey: bigint;    // Poseidon(privateKey, 0)
}

interface Utxo {
  amount: bigint;
  keypair: UtxoKeypair;
  blinding: bigint;
  mintAddress: PublicKey;       // NATIVE_SOL_MINT for SOL
  index?: number;               // leaf index after insertion
  commitment?: bigint;          // Poseidon(amount, pubkey, blinding, mintField)
  nullifier?: bigint;           // computed at spend time
  siblingCommitment?: bigint;   // other output from the same tx
}

// Exports:
const NATIVE_SOL_MINT: PublicKey;

function randomFieldElement(): bigint;
function generateUtxoKeypair(): Promise<UtxoKeypair>;
function deriveUtxoKeypairFromSpendKey(skSpend: Uint8Array): Promise<UtxoKeypair>;
function derivePublicKey(privateKey: bigint): Promise<bigint>;

function createUtxo(amount: bigint, keypair: UtxoKeypair, mint?: PublicKey): Promise<Utxo>;
function createZeroUtxo(mint?: PublicKey, salt?: bigint): Promise<Utxo>;

function pubkeyToFieldElement(pubkey: PublicKey): bigint;
function computeUtxoCommitment(utxo: Utxo): Promise<bigint>;
function computeSignature(privateKey: bigint, commitment: bigint, pathIndex: bigint): Promise<bigint>;
function computeUtxoNullifier(utxo: Utxo): Promise<bigint>;

function serializeUtxo(utxo: Utxo): Uint8Array;   // 128 bytes, little-endian
function deserializeUtxo(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<Utxo>;

function bigintToHex(value: bigint): string;
function utxoHexToBigint(hex: string): bigint;
function utxoBigintToBytes32(value: bigint): Uint8Array;

function sumUtxoAmounts(utxos: Utxo[]): bigint;
function selectUtxos(available: Utxo[], targetAmount: bigint): Utxo[] | null;
function utxoEquals(a: Utxo, b: Utxo): Promise<boolean>;

// Reconcile restored notes against chain before spending them. A note only lands in `unspent` or
// `spent` when it carries `commitment`, `mintAddress` AND a keypair; anything missing one of those
// lands in `skipped`, which means UNVERIFIED, not absent.
interface VerifyUtxosResult { spent: Utxo[]; unspent: Utxo[]; skipped: Utxo[]; }
function verifyUtxos(
  utxos: Utxo[], connection: Connection, programId: PublicKey,
  commitment?: "processed" | "confirmed" | "finalized",
): Promise<VerifyUtxosResult>;
function preflightNullifiers(                      // throws UtxoAlreadySpentError on a spent input
  utxos: Utxo[], connection: Connection, programId: PublicKey,
  commitment?: "processed" | "confirmed" | "finalized",
): Promise<void>;
```

`serializeUtxo` is the persistence primitive and it is the ONLY one: 128 bytes carrying amount,
private key, blinding, mint and index. Every flow hands back a note the SDK then forgets, with one
conditional exception below (a full withdrawal of one or two input notes), and `createUtxo` draws
that note's `blinding` from `randomFieldElement()` and writes it nowhere on chain, so a note that
is not serialized to durable storage before you report success is permanently unspendable by
anyone. `StorageAdapter` (§5.13) is a DIFFERENT boundary: its methods are typed on `CloakNote`, and
it does not accept these bytes.

**The full-withdrawal exemption is CONDITIONAL: it holds for one or two input notes only.**
`fullWithdraw` sums the inputs and calls `partialWithdraw`, and `partialWithdraw` runs
`while (utxos.length > 2)` first: it sorts the notes, merges the two smallest on chain into a fresh
note from `createUtxo`, and repeats until two remain. Each round nullifies its two inputs on chain
and the merged note's blinding exists only in that call's local variable. If a later round or the
final withdrawal throws (stale-root retries exhausted, a relay 5xx, a closed tab, a rejected wallet
approval), the spent inputs are gone, the merged commitment is on chain, and the call returns no
result to persist, so the balance is unrecoverable by anyone. There is no API that hands you the
intermediate note. Mitigations, in order: withdraw from at most two notes (consolidate deliberately
with your own `transact` calls, persisting each merged output, before calling `fullWithdraw`), and
watch `onProgress` for `Consolidating notes (n remaining)...`, which is the ONLY signal the caller
gets that consolidation is running. `partialWithdraw` shares the same loop and the same exposure.

### 5.3 UTXO transaction API (primary runtime path)

```ts
function transact(params: TransactParams, options: TransactOptions): Promise<TransactResult>;
function transfer(inputUtxos: Utxo[], recipientPubkey: bigint, amount: bigint, options: TransactOptions): Promise<TransactResult>;
function partialWithdraw(inputUtxos: Utxo[], recipient: PublicKey, withdrawAmount: bigint, options: TransactOptions): Promise<TransactResult>;
function fullWithdraw(inputUtxos: Utxo[], recipient: PublicKey, options: TransactOptions): Promise<TransactResult>;
function swapUtxo(params: UtxoSwapParams, options: TransactOptions): Promise<UtxoSwapResult>;
function swapWithChange(
  inputUtxos: Utxo[],
  swapAmount: bigint,
  outputMint: PublicKey,
  recipientAta: PublicKey,
  minOutputAmount: bigint,
  options: TransactOptions,
  recipientWallet?: PublicKey,
): Promise<UtxoSwapResult>;

// The swap result. It extends TransactResult, so it also carries `signature`, `outputUtxos`,
// `commitmentIndices`, `merkleTree` and the rest of that shape.
interface UtxoSwapResult extends TransactResult {
  swapStatePda: string;      // SwapState PDA, base58
  nullifier: string;         // hex nullifier the PDA is derived from
  requestId?: string;        // request id for polling swap execution status
  refund: {                  // the timeout-refund secret. MONEY. Persist it (see below).
    privateKey: string;      // hex 32-byte field elements, all three
    publicKey: string;
    blinding: string;
    derivedFromNk: boolean;  // true => also rediscoverable from `nk` (discoverSwapRefunds, §5.5)
  };
}

function computeExtDataHash(recipient: PublicKey | null, relayerFee: bigint, relayer: PublicKey | null, maxFee?: bigint): Promise<bigint>;

// Chain note v4. The tail binds noteSemantics = Poseidon(outAmount0, outPubkey0, isSendToSelfKey0)
// to match the ceremony circuit, so this is an EIGHT-argument hash, not four. `transact` computes
// it for you; there is no reason to call this in an integration.
function computeChainNoteHash(
  publicAmount: bigint, extDataHash: bigint, noteTimestamp: bigint, noteCommitment: bigint,
  noteSalt: bigint, outAmount0: bigint, outPubkey0: bigint, noteIsSendToSelfKey0: bigint,
): Promise<bigint>;

function setCircuitsPath(next: string): void;
function getCircuitsPath(): string | null;
function resolveCircuitsBase(explicit?: string): string; // explicit → CLOAK_CIRCUITS_PATH / CLOAK_CIRCUITS → pinned 0.2.0 default

function fetchRiskQuoteInstruction(
  riskQuoteUrl: string,
  wallet: PublicKey,
  options: {                       // REQUIRED, and `poolMint` inside it is required too
    poolMint: PublicKey;
    recipient?: PublicKey;
    amount?: bigint;
    token?: PublicKey;
    commitment?: string | Uint8Array;
    context?: "deposit" | "send" | "withdraw";
    nullifier0?: string;
    nullifier1?: string;
  },
): Promise<TransactionInstruction>;

const DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_URL: string | null; // ".../cloak-circuits/circuits/0.2.0" in 0.2.0
const TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_VERSION: "0.2.0";
```

**`UtxoSwapResult.refund` is the user's principal, not telemetry.** A swap locks the SOL in a
SwapState PDA and only settles on a second transaction. If it times out before that, the close path
returns the principal to the pool as an amount-bound note

```
R_fb = Poseidon(amountAfterFee, refund.publicKey, refund.blinding, WSOL)
```

where `amountAfterFee` is the amount the program actually locked, read authoritatively from the
on-chain `SwapState.sol_amount` (the gross swap amount minus the on-chain program fee). Claiming it
back requires `refund.privateKey`. Persist the whole `refund` object alongside the change note, in
the same tick `swapUtxo` / `swapWithChange` returns.

`derivedFromNk` says whether losing it is survivable. When it is `true`, the same secret can be
rebuilt later from the wallet's `nk` plus the swap's public first input nullifier, which is what
`discoverSwapRefunds` (§5.5) walks the chain for. When it is `false`, the returned object is the
only copy that will ever exist. The `nk` in question is `TransactOptions.chainNoteViewingKeyNk` when
you passed one; when you did not, the SDK falls back to
`getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey(inputUtxos[0].keypair.privateKey)`, so the recovery scan then needs that
same first input's private key. Pass an explicit `chainNoteViewingKeyNk` on every swap so the
recovery key is one you already hold. Persisting `refund` stays the fast path either way.

Key `TransactOptions` fields (most used):

```ts
interface TransactOptions {
  connection: Connection;
  programId: PublicKey;
  relayUrl?: string;                      // NO default, see §1; required on every flow.
                                          // Pass an allowlisted origin. "" is the caller-signed
                                          // direct-submission signal ONLY with
                                          // enforceViewingKeyRegistration: false; on default
                                          // options "" throws like omitting it (§1, invariant 7).

  // Signing. The RUNTIME picks the shape; it is not a free choice (invariant 13, §8 rule 15):
  //   NODE / SERVER: depositorKeypair + walletPublicKey.
  //   BROWSER:       signMessage + walletPublicKey on every relay-submitted flow (private send,
  //                  withdraw, swap), plus signTransaction + depositorPublicKey on a deposit.
  // A wallet adapter holds no secret key and can never produce a Keypair, so depositorKeypair in
  // browser code is code that cannot run. Never generate it there, and never ask a browser user
  // for a keypair.json path.
  depositorKeypair?: Keypair;             // NODE / SERVER ONLY. Unreachable from a wallet adapter.
  signTransaction?: WalletAdapter["signTransaction"]; // browser: signs the DEPOSIT transaction
  signMessage?: (msg: Uint8Array) => Promise<Uint8Array>; // browser: authenticates relay-submitted
                                          // flows AND the viewing-key challenge, so it is required
                                          // in the browser on every flow, deposits included.
  walletPublicKey?: PublicKey;            // the END USER'S real wallet, never an ephemeral or
                                          // service key. Passing depositorKeypair together with a
                                          // DIFFERENT walletPublicKey throws.
  depositorPublicKey?: PublicKey;

  // UX / observability:
  onProgress?: (status: string) => void;
  onProofProgress?: (percent: number) => void;

  // Retry + reliability:
  maxRootRetries?: number;
  retryDelayMs?: number;

  // Compliance / chain notes:
  chainNoteViewingKeyNk?: string | Uint8Array;
  getChainNoteViewingKeyNk?: () => Promise<string | Uint8Array | null>;
  chainNoteSalt?: bigint;                 // pin the note's 96-bit salt; pass the `noteSalt` from
                                          // createRecoverableDepositUtxo so a cold scan can rebuild
                                          // the deposit note (§5.5). Requires an explicit nk.
  recipientViewingPublicKey?: Uint8Array | string; // shield-to-shield ONLY: the RECIPIENT'S X25519
                                          // public viewing key, i.e.
                                          // deriveViewingKeyFromNk(recipientNk).publicKey. Without
                                          // it the send still succeeds but the recipient CANNOT
                                          // discover the note from chain (§5.5, §6.4).
  disableChainNotes?: boolean;            // drop the on-chain ciphertext blob only; the proof still
                                          // binds chainNoteHash. Costs auto-scan discovery.
  metadataBundle?: EncryptedMetadataBundle;
  encryptedNotes?: string[];
  enforceViewingKeyRegistration?: boolean;

  // Performance:
  cachedMerkleTree?: MerkleTree;
  useChainForMerkle?: boolean;
  useChainRootForProof?: boolean;
  useUniqueNullifiers?: boolean;

  // ALTs:
  altAddresses?: string[];
  addressLookupTableAccounts?: AddressLookupTableAccount[];

  // Swap-specific:
  maxWalletApprovals?: number;            // swaps ONLY: cap on wallet re-prompts (default 5,
                                          // floored at 1). Sends and withdrawals prompt once and
                                          // never consult this.
  swapDexes?: string[];
  swapExcludeDexes?: string[];
  swapRouteRetryAttempts?: number;
  swapMaxRetries?: number;
  swapSlippageBps?: number;
  swapStatusMaxAttempts?: number;
  swapStatusDelayMs?: number;

  // Risk oracle:
  riskOracleQueue?: PublicKey;
  riskQuoteUrl?: string;
  getRiskQuoteInstruction?: (wallet: PublicKey) => Promise<TransactionInstruction>; // one arg
  rangeApiKey?: string;
}
```

### 5.4 Chain-note encryption

`transact` builds and embeds the chain note itself when you pass `chainNoteViewingKeyNk`. These
exports exist for callers reading notes back. There is no `encodeCompactChainNote` /
`decodeCompactChainNote` in the public surface: encryption and encoding are the same call.

```ts
type ChainNoteTxType = "deposit" | "withdraw" | "transfer" | "swap" | "unknown";

interface CompactChainNote {
  timestamp: bigint;
  commitment: string;
  noteSalt?: bigint;        // v3+
  outAmount0?: bigint;      // v4 only: the three terms of noteSemantics
  outPubkey0?: bigint;
  isSendToSelfKey0?: bigint;
}

// Encrypt. Takes the note's parts, NOT a CompactChainNote, and the caller's `nk`, NOT a public
// key. Returns raw envelope BYTES, not base64.
function encryptCompactChainNote(
  timestamp: bigint,
  nk: Uint8Array,
  commitmentHex: string,
  noteSalt: bigint,
  semantics?: { outAmount0: bigint; outPubkey0: bigint; isSendToSelfKey0: bigint },
): Promise<Uint8Array>;

// Decrypt. The key is derived per output commitment, so you MUST supply the candidate commitments
// the transaction published; the call tries each until AES-GCM authenticates. Accepts v3 and
// legacy v2 notes. It is async.
function decryptCompactChainNote(
  noteBytes: Uint8Array,
  nk: Uint8Array,
  candidateCommitments: string[],
): Promise<CompactChainNote>;

// Transport only: these move ENVELOPE BYTES in and out of base64. Neither one parses a note.
function chainNoteToBase64(noteBytes: Uint8Array): string;
function chainNoteFromBase64(base64: string): Uint8Array;
```

For ordinary history and note recovery, do not drive these by hand: `scanTransactions` (§5.5) finds
the envelopes, supplies the candidate commitments and decrypts them for you.

### 5.5 Scanner / compliance

```ts
interface ScanOptions {
  connection: Connection;
  programId: PublicKey;
  viewingKeyNk: Uint8Array;
  limit?: number;
  afterTimestamp?: number;
  beforeTimestamp?: number;
  untilSignature?: string;
  onProgress?: (processed: number, total: number) => void;
  batchSize?: number;
  onStatus?: (status: string) => void;
  debug?: boolean;
  walletPublicKey?: string;
  includeRecipientDeliveries?: boolean; // sweep the CLKD1 delivery registry (default: true)
  ownerUtxoPublicKey?: bigint;          // this wallet's UTXO pubkey; without it deliveries arrive UNVERIFIED
  deliveryMints?: PublicKey[];          // candidate pool mints for that verification (default: native SOL)
}

interface ScannedTransaction {
  txType: ChainNoteTxType;
  amount: bigint;
  fee: bigint;
  netAmount: bigint;
  timestamp: bigint;       // ms
  recipient: string;       // base58
  commitment: string;      // hex
  signature: string;
  runningBalance: bigint;
  mint: string;
  decimals: number;
  symbol: string;
  outputMint?: string;     // swaps
  outputSymbol?: string;
}

interface ScanSummary {
  totalDeposits: bigint;
  totalWithdrawals: bigint;
  totalFees: bigint;
  netChange: bigint;
  transactionCount: number;
  finalBalance: bigint;
}

interface ScanResult {
  transactions: ScannedTransaction[];
  summary: ScanSummary;
  lastSignature?: string;
  rpcCallsMade: number;

  // Note RECOVERY. Additive by design: these carry SPENDABLE secrets, so they are deliberately
  // kept out of `transactions` / `summary` and the compliance report shape is unchanged.
  deliveredNotes: DeliveredNote[];
  recoveredDepositNotes: RecoveredDepositNoteRecord[];
}

// A note delivered TO the scanning wallet by SOMEONE ELSE'S shield-to-shield send.
interface DeliveredNote {
  commitment: string;          // lowercase hex, as the carrier declares it
  amount: bigint;              // decrypted from the envelope
  blinding: bigint;            // decrypted from the envelope
  carrierSignature: string;    // the discovery record, NOT the source transaction
  blockTime?: number;          // seconds, when the RPC supplied one
  mint?: string;               // resolved by recomputing; present only with `ownerUtxoPublicKey`
  commitmentVerified: boolean; // true ONLY when the commitment was recomputed and matched
}

// This wallet's OWN deposit, rebuilt in spendable form from `nk` alone.
interface RecoveredDepositNoteRecord {  // extends RecoveredDepositNote extends DepositNoteSecrets
  keypair: UtxoKeypair;
  blinding: bigint;
  amount: bigint;
  mintAddress: PublicKey;
  commitment: bigint;   // the published commitment, reproduced from the derived secrets
  noteSalt: bigint;     // the salt the chain note carried, which anchored the derivation
  signature: string;    // the deposit transaction
  timestamp: bigint;    // ms, from the chain note
}

// ComplianceReport is the JSON-safe version of ScanResult.
function scanTransactions(opts: ScanOptions): Promise<ScanResult>;
function toComplianceReport(result: ScanResult): ComplianceReport;
function formatComplianceCsv(report: ComplianceReport): string;

// Deposit-note recovery helpers (the builder side of `recoveredDepositNotes`).
function createRecoverableDepositUtxo(
  amount: bigint, viewingKeyNk: Uint8Array, mintAddress?: PublicKey, noteSalt?: bigint,
): Promise<{ utxo: Utxo; noteSalt: bigint }>;
function deriveDepositNoteSecrets(viewingKeyNk: Uint8Array, noteSalt: bigint): Promise<DepositNoteSecrets>;
function randomDepositNoteSalt(): bigint;

// Delivery-registry sweep on its own, when you do not want a full history scan. It resolves to a
// WRAPPER, not a bare array: read `.notes`. Its options name the mint list `mints`, not
// `deliveryMints` (that spelling belongs to `ScanOptions`).
function scanRecipientDeliveryNotes(
  opts: ScanRecipientDeliveryOptions,   // { connection, programId, viewingKeyNk,
                                        //   ownerUtxoPublicKey?, mints?, onStatus?, debug? }
): Promise<{ notes: DeliveredNote[]; rpcCalls: number }>;
```

**History is NOT recovery, and the two fields above are the exception.** Getting this wrong is how a
wallet loses funds, so do not generalise from either half of it:

- `transactions` is a HISTORY row. It records that a note existed and for how much. It carries no
  keypair and no blinding, so nothing in it can be spent. A UI can render it; a wallet cannot
  restore a balance from it.
- `deliveredNotes` IS spendable: notes other people sent to this wallet, opened from the CLKD1
  delivery registry with the scanning wallet's `nk`. The carrier memo's commitment field is
  unauthenticated, so treat a note as real only when `commitmentVerified === true`, which requires
  passing `ownerUtxoPublicKey` (and `deliveryMints` for a non-SOL pool) in `ScanOptions`. Without
  it, every delivered note comes back `commitmentVerified: false`.
- `recoveredDepositNotes` IS spendable: this wallet's own deposits, rebuilt from `nk` alone. ONLY
  deposits built with `createRecoverableDepositUtxo(...)` AND submitted with that same salt as
  `TransactOptions.chainNoteSalt` land here. A deposit whose blinding came from raw randomness has
  nothing to rebuild and appears as a history row only.
- NOTHING recovers a CHANGE note. `createUtxo` draws its blinding from `randomFieldElement()` and
  writes it nowhere, and the chain note carries no blinding, so the change output of a send, a
  partial withdraw or a swap is unrecoverable the moment it is dropped. Persist every output UTXO
  with `serializeUtxo` (§5.2) as soon as the call returns. Scanning will not bring it back.
- A swap's `UtxoSwapResult.refund` (§5.3) is a separate secret again, and it is the only way to
  claim the principal back if the swap times out. It is the one item on this list with a key-only
  fallback: `discoverSwapRefunds`, below, when the swap was built with an `nk`. Persist it anyway.

**Swap timeout-refund discovery.** The recovery path for a `UtxoSwapResult.refund` (§5.3) that was
never persisted: it rebuilds the stranded refund leaf from key material alone, with no relay, no
local note store and no prior knowledge of the swap.

```ts
interface SwapRefundAuthorization { privateKey: bigint; publicKey: bigint; blinding: bigint; }

interface RecoveredSwapRefund {
  keypair: UtxoKeypair;
  blinding: bigint;
  amount: bigint;
  commitment: bigint;        // R_fb, identical to the leaf the close path appended
}

interface DiscoveredSwapRefund extends RecoveredSwapRefund {
  signature: string;         // the close transaction that appended the leaf
  leafIndex: bigint;
  inputNullifier: Uint8Array; // first input nullifier of the swap this refund belongs to
  swapSignature?: string;    // the opening swap tx, when it fell inside the scanned window
}

function discoverSwapRefunds(
  connection: Connection,
  programId: PublicKey,
  viewingKeyNk: Uint8Array,             // the SAME nk the swap was built with (§5.3)
  options?: {
    limit?: number;                     // program signatures to walk; omit or 0 for all history
    untilSignature?: string;            // resume cursor from a previous run (exclusive)
    batchSize?: number;                 // getTransaction concurrency, default 50
    onStatus?: (status: string) => void;
    poolMint?: PublicKey;               // swap input is wSOL-locked; the SOL default is correct
  },
): Promise<DiscoveredSwapRefund[]>;

// The pieces it is built from, for a caller walking its own transactions instead.
function deriveSwapRefundAuthorization(
  viewingKeyNk: Uint8Array, inputNullifier: Uint8Array | bigint,
): Promise<SwapRefundAuthorization>;
function computeSwapRefundCommitment(
  amountAfterFee: bigint, refundPublicKey: bigint, refundBlinding: bigint,
): Promise<bigint>;
function matchSwapRefundLeaf(params: {
  viewingKeyNk: Uint8Array;
  inputNullifier: Uint8Array | bigint;  // read from the swap's public inputs
  amountAfterFee: bigint;               // the principal the close path returned
  commitment: bigint | Uint8Array;      // R_fb as appended on chain
}): Promise<RecoveredSwapRefund | null>; // null for every leaf that is not this wallet's
```

An empty result is NOT proof that a wallet has no stranded refund. `discoverSwapRefunds` finds only
refunds whose authorization was DERIVED from an `nk`. A swap whose refund keypair and blinding came
from raw randomness has no derivation to replay, and no key-only scan will ever find it; for those,
the in-memory `UtxoSwapResult.refund` was the only copy. Never report "no stranded refunds" on the
strength of an empty return.

```ts
function deriveViewingKeyFromSpendKey(skSpend: Uint8Array): ViewingKeyPair;

function getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey(utxoPrivateKey: bigint): Uint8Array;

function deriveDiversifier(nk: Uint8Array, commitmentHex: string, outputIndex: number): Uint8Array; // 11 bytes
function deriveDiversifiedViewingKey(nk: Uint8Array, diversifier: Uint8Array): ViewingKeyPair;

function generateViewingKeyPair(): ViewingKeyPair;
function registerViewingKey(
  relayUrl: string,
  userPubkey: PublicKey,
  nk: Uint8Array,

const SIGN_IN_MESSAGE: string;
```
