### 5.8 Relay + merkle + on-chain proof helpers

```ts
// Every params shape below is declared INLINE on the class. There is no exported
// `SubmitWithdrawParams` / `SubmitSwapParams` type name to import.
class RelayService {
  constructor(baseUrl: string);

  submitWithdraw(
    params: {
      proof: string;
      publicInputs: { root: string; nf: string; outputs_hash: string; amount: number };
      outputs: Array<{ recipient: string; amount: number }>;
      feeBps: number;
      metadataBundle?: EncryptedMetadataBundle;
    },
    onStatusUpdate?: (status: string) => void,
    onRequestId?: (requestId: string) => void,
  ): Promise<string>;

  submitSwap(
    params: {
      proof: string;
      publicInputs: { root: string; nf: string; outputs_hash: string; amount: number };
      outputs: Array<{ recipient: string; amount: number }>;
      feeBps: number;
      swap: { output_mint: string; slippage_bps: number; min_output_amount: number };
      metadataBundle?: EncryptedMetadataBundle;
    },
    onStatusUpdate?: (status: string) => void,
    onRequestId?: (requestId: string) => void,
  ): Promise<string>;

  resumeWithdraw(requestId: string, onStatusUpdate?: (status: string) => void): Promise<{
    status: "completed" | "failed" | "pending"; signature?: string; error?: string;
  }>;
  getStatus(requestId: string): Promise<TxStatus>;
  registerViewingKey(userPubkey: string, viewingKey: string, signMessage: (msg: Uint8Array) => Promise<Uint8Array>): Promise<boolean>;
  getCompliancePublicKey(): Promise<Uint8Array>;
}

function fetchCommitments(relayUrl: string, options?: {
  mint?: PublicKey;
  timeoutMs?: number;
  maxRetries?: number;
  sync?: boolean;
  repair?: boolean;
  requireTarget?: boolean;
  requireCanonical?: boolean;
  fromIndex?: number;
  limit?: number;
  waitForIndex?: number;
}): Promise<CommitmentEntry[]>;

function buildMerkleTreeFromRelay(relayUrl: string, options?: {
  mint?: PublicKey;
  sync?: boolean;
  repair?: boolean;
  requireTarget?: boolean;
  requireCanonical?: boolean;
  timeoutMs?: number;
  maxRetries?: number;
  waitForIndex?: number;
}): Promise<MerkleTree>;

function buildMerkleTreeFromChain(
  connection: Connection,
  programId: PublicKey,
  merkleTree: PublicKey,
  onProgress?: (m: string) => void,
  mint?: PublicKey,        // required in practice: without it a CloseSwapState refund leaf
                           // cannot be attributed to a tree and reconstruction fails closed
): Promise<MerkleTree>;

function validateRoot(relayUrl: string, rootHex: string): Promise<{ valid: boolean; currentRoot?: string; message: string; isRecent: boolean; }>;
function waitForRoot(relayUrl: string, rootHex: string, timeoutMs?: number, pollIntervalMs?: number): Promise<{ success: boolean; currentRoot?: string; waitedMs: number; }>;
function preflightCheck(relayUrl: string, rootHex: string): Promise<{
  shouldProceed: boolean;
  action: "proceed" | "refresh_proofs" | "rebuild_tree" | "wait";
  message: string;
  estimatedWaitMs?: number;
}>;

function readMerkleTreeState(
  connection: Connection,
  merkleTreePDA: PublicKey,
  forceConfirmed?: boolean,
  relayUrl?: string,
  skipRelayRoot?: boolean,
  mint?: PublicKey,
): Promise<{ nextIndex: number; root: string; subtrees: string[] }>;

function computeProofFromChain(connection: Connection, merkleTreePDA: PublicKey, leafIndex: number, forceConfirmed?: boolean): Promise<OnchainMerkleProof>;
function computeProofForLatestDeposit(connection: Connection, merkleTreePDA: PublicKey): Promise<OnchainMerkleProof & { leafIndex: number }>;
```

**Request authentication (all exported).** Standard integrations never call these: pass `signMessage` + `walletPublicKey` (browser) or `depositorKeypair` (server) in `TransactOptions` and the SDK signs for you. These exist for callers driving submission themselves.

```ts
// Endpoint pinning
const CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL = "https://api.cloak.ag"; // a NAME, never a default
const RELAY_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST: readonly string[];           // origins THIS build may reach
const BUILD_ALLOWS_LOCAL_ENDPOINTS: boolean;               // derived; true only for a local build

// Freshness window
const REQUEST_AUTH_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 300;         // usable budget is 285 (15s held back for transit)
const REQUEST_AUTH_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECONDS = 30;  // a clock this far FAST cannot authenticate

// The exact fields each body signs, sorted; order is part of the agreement
const TRANSACT_AUTH_FIELDS: readonly ["encrypted_notes","max_fee","mint","proof_bytes","public_inputs","recipient","recipient_delivery_notes","risk_quote","sender"];
const TRANSACT_SWAP_AUTH_FIELDS: readonly ["close_timed_out","dexes","encrypted_notes","exclude_dexes","max_fee","min_output_amount","output_mint","proof_bytes","public_inputs","recipient","recipient_ata","refund_blinding","refund_pubkey","retry_request_id","risk_quote","route_retry_attempts","sender","slippage_bps","swap_max_retries"];

interface RelayAuthPreimage { sender: string; auth_issued_at: string; auth_nonce: string; message: Uint8Array; }
interface RelayAuthSigner  { walletPublicKey: PublicKey; signMessage: (m: Uint8Array) => Promise<Uint8Array>; }

function buildRelayAuthPreimage(
  endpoint: string,            // the exact path POSTed to, e.g. "/transact"
  programId: PublicKey,
  body: Record<string, unknown>,
  sender: PublicKey,           // the END USER'S wallet; becomes `sender`
  nowSeconds?: number,
  fields?: readonly string[],  // TRANSACT_AUTH_FIELDS (default) | TRANSACT_SWAP_AUTH_FIELDS
): RelayAuthPreimage;

function canonicalJson(value: unknown): string;                  // keys sorted bytewise, no whitespace
function explainRelayAuthRejection(responseText: string): string | null;
function submitTransactToRelay(                  // takes depositorKeypair | relayAuthSigner
  args: SubmitTransactToRelayArgs,
): Promise<RelaySubmissionResult>;

type RelaySubmissionResult =
  | { kind: "submitted"; signature: string; commitmentIndices?: [number, number];
      viewingKeyRegistered?: boolean; settlement: SettlementVerdict }
  | { kind: "stale-root"; error: Error }   // root rejected; rebuild the tree and re-prove
  | { kind: "failed"; error: Error };

interface SettlementVerdict {
  status: "landed" | "failed" | "not-landed" | "unknown";
  signature: string | null;
  reason: string;                          // safe to put in an error message
  nullifiersSpent: boolean;                // true when every checkable nullifier PDA was on chain
  signatureStatus: "finalized" | "confirmed" | "processed" | "absent" | "error" | "unchecked";
}
```

Branch on `kind`; the three outcomes above are returned, not thrown. A `"submitted"` result is not
by itself proof: read `settlement.status`, and never report `"unknown"` as success or silently
retry it. Surface `settlement.signature` instead.

`preimage.message` is a plain ed25519 detached-signature preimage, newline separated:

```
CLOAK_RELAY_REQUEST_AUTH_V1
<endpoint>
<program id, base58>
<auth_nonce>
<auth_issued_at>
<sha256 hex of canonicalJson(signed view)>
```

Put `sender`, `auth_issued_at`, `auth_nonce` from the preimage plus the base64 signature as `auth_signature` on the POSTed body. Re-POSTing a request MUST reuse the same preimage and the same body bytes; rebuilding it produces a new request, not a retry.

HARD TRAP: `slippage_bps` MUST always be present in a signed swap body. Every other field in both lists signs as an explicit `null` when absent, but `slippage_bps` is a bare `u16` with a default of `500` on the receiving side, so omitting it signs `null` against a signed `500`. The digests diverge and the rejection never mentions slippage. `buildRelayAuthPreimage` refuses the call rather than sign a digest that cannot match.

### 5.9 Proof / circuit utilities

This SDK pins exactly ONE circuit: the ceremony-frozen `transaction` circuit. The pre-ceremony
`withdraw_regular` / `withdraw_swap` circuits were removed in 0.2.0 together with every function
that loaded them, so proof generation is not a public entry point at all. There is no
`generateWithdrawRegularProof`, `generateWithdrawSwapProof`, `areCircuitsAvailable` or
`getDefaultCircuitsPath`, and no `WithdrawRegularInputs` / `WithdrawSwapInputs` / `ProofResult`
type. `transact` and the flows built on it load, verify and prove for you; the exports below exist
for start-up diagnostics and for callers driving artifact loading themselves.

```ts
// Load artifacts and get back the very bytes whose digest was checked. Fails closed on any
// mismatch, unreachable artifact, or environment that cannot produce bytes. `circuitsPath` is a
// base directory or URL, honoured verbatim; pass `null` to report the "no base configured" state.
function loadVerifiedCircuitArtifacts(circuitsPath: string | null): Promise<{
  wasm: Uint8Array;
  zkey: Uint8Array;
  digests: { wasm: string; zkey: string };  // SHA-256 of the buffers in this same object
}>;   // the return shape is declared inline; it is NOT an exported type name

// The fail-closed gate: throws when the artifacts are not the pinned ones.
function assertTransactionCircuitIntegrity(
  circuitsPath: string | null,
  prefetched?: { wasm: Uint8Array; zkey: Uint8Array },   // already-downloaded bytes, to skip a refetch
): Promise<void>;

// Reporting only. These do NOT gate proving: a check that re-reads the source cannot speak for the
// bytes a later, independent read returns. Prove from loadVerifiedCircuitArtifacts, always.
function verifyCircuitIntegrity(
  circuitsPath: string | null,
  prefetched?: { wasm: Uint8Array; zkey: Uint8Array },
): Promise<CircuitVerificationResult>;
function verifyAllCircuits(
  circuitsPath: string | null,
  transactionCircuitsPath?: string | null,   // same base; takes precedence when given
): Promise<CircuitVerificationResult[]>;     // one entry, for `transaction`

interface CircuitVerificationResult {
  valid: boolean;
  error?: string;
  computed?: { wasm: string; zkey: string };
  expected?: { wasm: string; zkey: string };
}

const DEFAULT_CIRCUITS_URL: string; // alias of DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_URL: same ceremony transaction bundle, same 0.2.0 URL, never null
const EXPECTED_CIRCUIT_HASHES: Readonly<{   // frozen VIEW; exactly two keys, no withdraw_* entries
  transaction_wasm: string; // 02ec02e954ae3932827ad9de51afa597ca95569aa97fec8410879c937a58aa2b
  transaction_zkey: string; // 9da7db8cb1370fc497d36a0365f1f107ab0b0c13ca66fa9f0287e5f96ee68d25
}>;
```

There is no environment variable that disables the integrity check. A build that genuinely needs
different artifacts needs different DIGESTS, which is a source edit and a rebuild, exactly like the
endpoint pin.

The `transaction` circuit (used by `transact`, `transfer`, `partialWithdraw`, `fullWithdraw`, `swapUtxo`, `swapWithChange`) is frozen by the `cloak-transaction-0.2.0` trusted-setup ceremony. The SDK checks every artifact it loads against these digests and refuses to prove against anything else; the program rejects proofs from the older `0.1.0` bundle.

### 5.10 Wallet helpers

```ts
function validateWalletConnected(wallet: WalletAdapter | Keypair): void;
function getPublicKey(wallet: WalletAdapter | Keypair): PublicKey;
function sendTransaction(
  tx: Transaction,
  wallet: WalletAdapter | Keypair,
  connection: Connection,
  options?: SendOptions,
): Promise<string>;
function signTransaction<T extends Transaction>(tx: T, wallet: WalletAdapter | Keypair): Promise<T>;
function keypairToAdapter(keypair: Keypair): WalletAdapter;
```

`UtxoWallet` and `SimpleWallet` are also exported and are NOT send paths. `UtxoWallet.prepareSend`
and `SimpleWallet.send` build the recipient output from a freshly generated random keypair, so the
recipient cannot spend what they produce, and `SimpleWallet.sync()` throws
`Sync not yet implemented`. `UtxoWallet.serialize()` additionally drops each note's `commitment`,
so notes restored from it come back from `verifyUtxos` (§5.2) as `skipped`. Use `transfer` for a
shielded send and `fullWithdraw` / `partialWithdraw` to exit the pool.

### 5.11 Fees

Fees are enforced on-chain by the program from each pool's `PoolConfig`; `transact` reads the live
config before building a fee-bearing proof, so you do not compute the fee yourself. The helpers
below use the deployed SOL-pool defaults (`5_000_000` lamports fixed + `3 / 1000`):

```ts
const FIXED_FEE_LAMPORTS: number;      // 5_000_000
const MIN_DEPOSIT_LAMPORTS: number;    // 10_000_000
const VARIABLE_FEE_NUMERATOR: number;  // 3
const VARIABLE_FEE_DENOMINATOR: number;// 1000
const VARIABLE_FEE_RATE: number;       // 0.003

// SOL pool. These four functions are the entire fee surface the SDK exports.
function calculateFee(amountLamports: number): number;          // fixed + variable
function calculateFeeBigint(amountLamports: bigint): bigint;    // same, bigint
function isWithdrawAmountSufficient(amountLamports: bigint): boolean;
function getDistributableAmount(amountLamports: number): number;

// Formatting
function formatAmount(lamports: number, decimals?: number): string;
function parseAmount(sol: string): number;
```

There is NO SPL fee helper. USDC and USDT pools charge `450_000` base units fixed (0.45 token at
6 decimals) plus the same `3 / 1000` variable fee in the withdrawn token, and the program reads the
effective values from the `pool_config` PDA; minimum SPL deposit is `1_000_000` base units (1.00).
Compute an SPL fee yourself, or read it back from the transaction result. Do not invent a
`calculateSpl*` or Q64 helper: none exists. See `/protocol/fee-model`.

### 5.12 Errors

```ts
class RootNotFoundError extends Error {}
function isRootNotFoundError(error: unknown): boolean;

const ShieldPoolErrors: Record<number, string>; // maps 0x1000+ program error codes to human strings
function parseError(error: unknown): UserFriendlyError;
function parseTransactionError(error: any): string;
function formatErrorForLogging(error: unknown): string;
function parseRelayErrorResponse(text: string): { isRootNotFound: boolean; currentRoot?: string };
```

### 5.13 Network + logging + storage + PDAs

```ts
function detectNetworkFromRpcUrl(rpcUrl?: string): Network;
function getRpcUrlForNetwork(network: Network): string;
function isValidRpcUrl(url: string): boolean;
function getExplorerUrl(signature: string, network?: Network): string;
function getAddressExplorerUrl(address: string, network?: Network): string;

function createLogger(module: string): Logger;
function setDebugMode(enabled: boolean): void;
function formatSol(lamports: number | bigint): string;
const sdkLogger: Logger;

// StorageAdapter stores `CloakNote` records and a `CloakKeyPair`. It does NOT store `Utxo`
// objects, and it does not accept the bytes `serializeUtxo` returns; those are your own store's
// problem (§9.3).
interface StorageAdapter {
  saveNote(note: CloakNote): Promise<void> | void;
  loadAllNotes(): Promise<CloakNote[]> | CloakNote[];
  updateNote(commitment: string, updates: Partial<CloakNote>): Promise<void> | void;
  deleteNote(commitment: string): Promise<void> | void;
  clearAllNotes(): Promise<void> | void;
  saveKeys(keys: CloakKeyPair): Promise<void> | void;
  loadKeys(): Promise<CloakKeyPair | null> | CloakKeyPair | null;
  deleteKeys(): Promise<void> | void;
}

class MemoryStorageAdapter implements StorageAdapter {}   // in-process; lost on reload
class LocalStorageAdapter implements StorageAdapter {
  constructor(notesKey?: string, keysKey?: string); // defaults: "cloak_notes", "cloak_wallet_keys"
}

function getShieldPoolPDAs(programId?: PublicKey, mint?: PublicKey): {
  pool: PublicKey; merkleTree: PublicKey; vaultAuthority: PublicKey; treasury: PublicKey;
};
function getNullifierPDA(poolPubkey: PublicKey, nullifier: Uint8Array | Buffer, programId?: PublicKey): [PublicKey, number];
function getSwapStatePDA(poolPubkey: PublicKey, nullifier: Uint8Array | Buffer, programId?: PublicKey): [PublicKey, number];
```

### 5.14 Pending operations persistence (browser-only)

```ts
function savePendingDeposit(p: PendingDeposit): void;
function loadPendingDeposits(): PendingDeposit[];
function updatePendingDeposit(commitment: string, updates: Partial<PendingDeposit>): void;
function removePendingDeposit(commitment: string): void;
function clearPendingDeposits(): void;

function savePendingWithdrawal(w: PendingWithdrawal): void;
function loadPendingWithdrawals(): PendingWithdrawal[];
function updatePendingWithdrawal(requestId: string, updates: Partial<PendingWithdrawal>): void;
function removePendingWithdrawal(requestId: string): void;
function clearPendingWithdrawals(): void;

function hasPendingOperations(): boolean;
function getPendingOperationsSummary(): {
  deposits: PendingDeposit[]; withdrawals: PendingWithdrawal[]; totalPending: number;
};
function cleanupStalePendingOperations(maxAgeMs?: number): {
  removedDeposits: number; removedWithdrawals: number;
};
```

---

## 6. Copy-paste recipes (Node/server form by default, browser form on every flow)

**Read this before copying any recipe in section 6.** Every recipe below is written in the
NODE / SERVER form, and `depositorKeypair: sender` is the field that makes it one. It is NOT the
browser form. A wallet adapter holds no secret key and can never produce a `Keypair`, so a recipe
pasted verbatim into browser code is code that cannot run. Each recipe therefore carries its own
browser block: never infer a recipe's signing shape from a neighbouring one.

The swap is always the same one field:

- Relay-submitted flows (private send, withdraw, swap):
  Node `depositorKeypair: sender` -> browser `signMessage: wallet.signMessage!` plus
  `walletPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet)`.
- Deposit (`externalAmount > 0n`, signed by the user straight to chain):
  Node `depositorKeypair: sender` -> browser `signTransaction: wallet.signTransaction!` plus
  `signMessage: wallet.signMessage!` plus `depositorPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet)`.

`signMessage` is required in the browser on EVERY flow, deposits included, because the mandatory
viewing-key registration signs a challenge before anything else happens (invariant 7). Guard on
`wallet.signMessage` being present before offering the action, and never mix a `depositorKeypair`
with a different `walletPublicKey`: they are two names for the same end user, and splitting them
throws.

`relayUrl` has no default and is REQUIRED on every recipe here, deposits included. Omit it and the
call throws `Viewing key registration is mandatory: relayUrl is required.` before any network call.
Pass the allowlisted origin by name (§1); never type a host.

All recipes assume you created:

```ts
import { CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID, CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL, getPublicKey } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";
import { Connection } from "@solana/web3.js";

const connection = new Connection(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!, "confirmed");
const programId  = CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID;
const relayUrl   = CLOAK_PRODUCTION_RELAY_URL;

// Node / server: `sender` is a Keypair.
// Browser: `wallet` is the object from useWallet(); see §4b.

// YOUR durable note store. Every recipe below writes through it; the SDK ships nothing that plays
// this role for `Utxo` bytes (`StorageAdapter` is a different boundary, §5.13). Back it with
// something that survives a process restart, and write BEFORE reporting success.
declare function saveNoteBytes(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;
declare function saveSwapRefund(refund: {
  privateKey: string; publicKey: string; blinding: string; derivedFromNk: boolean;
}): Promise<void>;
```

### 6.1 Deposit into a fresh UTXO (SOL)

```ts
import {
  NATIVE_SOL_MINT, createUtxo, createZeroUtxo, generateUtxoKeypair,
  getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey, serializeUtxo, transact,
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const amount = 1_000_000_000n; // 1 SOL

const utxoKeypair = await generateUtxoKeypair();
const depositUtxo = await createUtxo(amount, utxoKeypair, NATIVE_SOL_MINT);
const padding     = await createZeroUtxo();
const nk          = getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey(utxoKeypair.privateKey);

const depositResult = await transact(
  {
    inputUtxos:   [padding],
    outputUtxos:  [depositUtxo],
    externalAmount: amount,           // > 0 => deposit
    depositor:    sender.publicKey,
  },
  {
    connection,
    programId,
    relayUrl,                         // required even here; the viewing-key gate runs first
    depositorKeypair: sender,         // NODE ONLY
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
    onProgress: (s) => console.log("deposit:", s),
    onProofProgress: (p) => console.log("proof", p),
  },
);

console.log("tx", depositResult.signature);
console.log("leaf_index", depositResult.outputUtxos[0].index);

// This note was built with createUtxo, so its blinding is raw randomness and no scan rebuilds it.
// The returned UTXO already carries its leaf index; persist it as it stands.
await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(depositResult.outputUtxos[0]));
```

**Browser form of this same deposit.** A deposit is signed by the user's wallet and submitted
straight to chain, so it is the one flow that needs `signTransaction` as well as `signMessage`:

```ts
import { getPublicKey, serializeUtxo, transact } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const depositResult = await transact(
  {
    inputUtxos:   [padding],
    outputUtxos:  [depositUtxo],
    externalAmount: amount,
    depositor:    getPublicKey(wallet),
  },
  {
    connection,
    programId,
    relayUrl,
    signTransaction: wallet.signTransaction!,   // signs the deposit transaction
    signMessage: wallet.signMessage!,           // signs the viewing-key challenge
    depositorPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
  },
);

await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(depositResult.outputUtxos[0]));   // same rule here.
```

To make this deposit recoverable from `nk` alone later, build the output with
`createRecoverableDepositUtxo` and pass the salt it returns as `chainNoteSalt` (§5.5). Both forms
above draw a random salt, which leaves the note discoverable only from your own storage.

### 6.2 Full withdraw (spend the entire shielded balance)

```ts
import { fullWithdraw } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const withdrawResult = await fullWithdraw(
  [depositResult.outputUtxos[0]],
  recipient.publicKey,
  {
    connection,
    programId,
    relayUrl,
    depositorKeypair: sender,          // NODE ONLY; also signs the viewing-key challenge
    walletPublicKey: sender.publicKey,
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
    cachedMerkleTree: depositResult.merkleTree,
    onProgress: (s) => console.log("withdraw:", s),
  },
);
console.log("withdraw sig", withdrawResult.signature);
```

**Browser form of this same withdrawal.** A withdrawal is relay-submitted: no `Keypair`, no
`signTransaction`, and the wallet prompts EXACTLY ONCE no matter how many times the network is
retried.

```ts
import { fullWithdraw, getPublicKey } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const withdrawResult = await fullWithdraw(
  [depositResult.outputUtxos[0]],
  recipientPublicKey,
  {
    connection,
    programId,
    relayUrl,
    signMessage: wallet.signMessage!,          // authenticates the request; prompts once
    walletPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
    cachedMerkleTree: depositResult.merkleTree,
  },
);
```

The signed request is good for 285 usable seconds (§5.8). If the user leaves the approval dialog
open longer than that, map the rejection through `explainRelayAuthRejection` and ask again.

**Both forms above pass ONE input note, which is the only shape with nothing to persist.** Passing
three or more inputs makes `fullWithdraw` consolidate them on chain first, two at a time, and a
throw partway through strands the merged balance with no result to save (§5.2). Consolidate
deliberately with your own `transact` calls, persisting each merged output, or accept the risk
knowingly and watch `onProgress` for `Consolidating notes (n remaining)...`.

### 6.3 Partial withdraw (keep a shielded change UTXO)

```ts
import { partialWithdraw, serializeUtxo } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const withdrawAmount = 500_000_000n; // 0.5 SOL

const result = await partialWithdraw(
  [depositResult.outputUtxos[0]],
  recipient.publicKey,
  withdrawAmount,
  {
    connection,
    programId,
    relayUrl,
    depositorKeypair: sender,          // NODE ONLY
    walletPublicKey: sender.publicKey,
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
    cachedMerkleTree: depositResult.merkleTree,
  },
);

// result.outputUtxos[0] is the new shielded change UTXO (remainder), and this write is the only
// thing that keeps it spendable. Do it before you report success.
await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(result.outputUtxos[0]));
```

**Browser form of this same partial withdrawal.** Relay-submitted, so the keypair is replaced, not
supplemented:

```ts
import { getPublicKey, partialWithdraw, serializeUtxo } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const result = await partialWithdraw(
  [depositResult.outputUtxos[0]],
  recipientPublicKey,
  withdrawAmount,
  {
    connection,
    programId,
    relayUrl,
    signMessage: wallet.signMessage!,
    walletPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
    cachedMerkleTree: depositResult.merkleTree,
  },
);

await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(result.outputUtxos[0]));   // the change note. Same rule here.
```

**Persist `result.outputUtxos[0]` before you do anything else, in either form.** A change note is
the one thing NOTHING recovers: its blinding comes from `randomFieldElement()` and is written
nowhere on chain, so scanning will never bring it back (§5.5). Store it with `serializeUtxo`
(§5.2) the moment the call returns.

### 6.4 Shield-to-shield transfer / private send (publicAmount = 0)

Relay-submitted, so this recipe has a browser form and the block below is NOT it. In the browser
this flow uses `signMessage` + `walletPublicKey`; there is no `depositorKeypair` in browser code.

```ts
import { NATIVE_SOL_MINT, createUtxo, serializeUtxo, transact } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const transferAmount = 1_000_000_000n;
const changeAmount   = senderShieldedUtxo.amount - transferAmount;

const recipientOutput = await createUtxo(transferAmount, recipientUtxoKeypair, NATIVE_SOL_MINT);
const changeOutput    = await createUtxo(changeAmount,   senderUtxoKeypair,    NATIVE_SOL_MINT);

const result = await transact(
  {
    inputUtxos:  [senderShieldedUtxo],
    outputUtxos: [recipientOutput, changeOutput],
    externalAmount: 0n,    // shield-to-shield
  },
  {
    connection, programId,
    relayUrl,
    depositorKeypair: sender,          // NODE ONLY
    walletPublicKey: sender.publicKey,
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: senderNk,
    recipientViewingPublicKey,         // see "make the note discoverable" below
    cachedMerkleTree: senderCachedTree,
  },
);

// outputUtxos[1] is YOUR change (outputs were [recipientOutput, changeOutput]). Nothing on chain
// carries its blinding, so this write is the only thing that keeps it spendable.
await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(result.outputUtxos[1]));
```

**Browser form of this same private send.** Same call, same params, one field swapped. The wallet
prompts EXACTLY ONCE; a send never re-prompts on retry.

```ts
import { getPublicKey, serializeUtxo, transact } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const result = await transact(
  {
    inputUtxos:  [senderShieldedUtxo],
    outputUtxos: [recipientOutput, changeOutput],
    externalAmount: 0n,
  },
  {
    connection,
    programId,
    relayUrl,
    signMessage: wallet.signMessage!,          // authenticates /transact; prompts once
    walletPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: senderNk,
    recipientViewingPublicKey,
    cachedMerkleTree: senderCachedTree,
  },
);

await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(result.outputUtxos[1]));   // your change note. Same rule here.
```

`transfer(inputUtxos, recipientPubkey, amount, options)` (§5.3) wraps the same flow when you have
the recipient's UTXO public key as a `bigint` and want the SDK to build both outputs. Its
`options` argument is the identical `TransactOptions`, so the same Node-vs-browser swap applies.

**Make the note discoverable, or the recipient cannot spend it.** Pass
`recipientViewingPublicKey: deriveViewingKeyFromNk(recipientNk).publicKey` (hex or bytes) in
`TransactOptions`. The SDK then seals `{amount, blinding}` of output 0 to that key and ships it as
`recipient_delivery_notes`, which is what the recipient's `scanTransactions` later returns in
`ScanResult.deliveredNotes` (§5.5). Leave it out and the send still succeeds, but the recipient has
no way to find the note from chain and it must be handed over out of band.

And persist `changeOutput` yourself, in either form. Nothing recovers a change note (§5.5).

### 6.5 Fast send (deposit + full withdraw in one user action)

This is the ONE shape in section 6 that needs no note storage, and only because it is written the
way it is: exactly one deposit note goes in, `fullWithdraw` spends it in the same process, and a
one-input full withdrawal leaves no change. Every other recipe here writes a note before it reports
success. Do NOT generalise the recipe to a wallet's whole note set: pass three or more inputs and
`fullWithdraw` consolidates them on chain first, and a throw partway through strands the merged
balance with nothing to persist (§5.2). This shape stays storage-free only at one or two inputs.

```ts
import {
  NATIVE_SOL_MINT, createUtxo, createZeroUtxo, fullWithdraw,
  generateUtxoKeypair, getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey, transact,
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const amount = 1_000_000_000n;
const kp = await generateUtxoKeypair();
const utxo = await createUtxo(amount, kp, NATIVE_SOL_MINT);
const nk = getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey(kp.privateKey);

const dep = await transact(
  { inputUtxos: [await createZeroUtxo()], outputUtxos: [utxo], externalAmount: amount, depositor: sender.publicKey },
  { connection, programId, relayUrl, depositorKeypair: sender, chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk },  // NODE ONLY
);

const wd = await fullWithdraw([dep.outputUtxos[0]], recipient.publicKey, {
  connection, programId, relayUrl,
  depositorKeypair: sender,          // NODE ONLY
  walletPublicKey: sender.publicKey,
  chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
  cachedMerkleTree: dep.merkleTree,
});
```

**Browser form.** Two different swaps in one flow, because the two legs submit differently: the
deposit is signed to chain, the withdraw goes through the relay. That is two wallet prompts for the
deposit (`signTransaction` for the transaction, `signMessage` for the viewing-key challenge, the
latter only on first use per wallet) and exactly one more for the withdraw.

```ts
import {
  createZeroUtxo,
  fullWithdraw,
  getPublicKey,
  serializeUtxo,
  transact,
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const dep = await transact(
  { inputUtxos: [await createZeroUtxo()], outputUtxos: [utxo], externalAmount: amount, depositor: getPublicKey(wallet) },
  {
    connection, programId, relayUrl,
    signTransaction: wallet.signTransaction!,
    signMessage: wallet.signMessage!,
    depositorPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
  },
);

// Persist BEFORE the second leg. In a browser the process is a tab, and the withdraw
// below opens a wallet dialog: if the tab closes there, this note is the only claim on
// the funds already in the pool. saveNoteBytes is your storage, not an SDK export.
await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(dep.outputUtxos[0]));

const wd = await fullWithdraw([dep.outputUtxos[0]], recipientPublicKey, {
  connection, programId, relayUrl,
  signMessage: wallet.signMessage!,
  walletPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
  chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
  cachedMerkleTree: dep.merkleTree,
});
```

### 6.6 Swap SOL -> SPL (with shielded change)

```ts
import { NATIVE_SOL_MINT, serializeUtxo, swapWithChange } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";
import { PublicKey } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { getAssociatedTokenAddress } from "@solana/spl-token";
import { createJupiterApiClient } from "@jup-ag/api";

const swapAmount = 250_000_000n;                       // 0.25 SOL
const outputMint = new PublicKey("EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v"); // USDC
const recipientAta = await getAssociatedTokenAddress(outputMint, sender.publicKey);

// Quote (Jupiter) -> pick minOut:
const jup = createJupiterApiClient();
const quote = await jup.quoteGet({
  inputMint: NATIVE_SOL_MINT.toBase58(),   // swap input is wSOL-locked
  outputMint: outputMint.toBase58(),
  amount: Number(swapAmount),
  slippageBps: 1500,
});
const minOut = BigInt(quote.otherAmountThreshold);

const swapResult = await swapWithChange(
  depositResult.outputUtxos,   // inputs (must sum to >= swapAmount)
  swapAmount,
  outputMint,
  recipientAta,
  minOut,
  {
    connection, programId,
    relayUrl,
    depositorKeypair: sender,          // NODE ONLY
    walletPublicKey: sender.publicKey,
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
    cachedMerkleTree: depositResult.merkleTree,
    swapSlippageBps: 1500,
    swapStatusMaxAttempts: 60,
    swapStatusDelayMs: 2000,
  },
  sender.publicKey,            // so the SDK can create ATA if missing
);

console.log("swap sig", swapResult.signature);
console.log("swapStatePda", swapResult.swapStatePda);

// TWO pieces of the user's own money exist only in that returned object. Write both now.
await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(swapResult.outputUtxos[0]));  // shielded change note
await saveSwapRefund(swapResult.refund);                        // timeout-refund secret
```

**Browser form of this same swap.** Relay-submitted, so the same one-field swap, with one extra
thing to plan for in the UI: a swap is the ONLY flow that can re-prompt the wallet, because a
route can be re-quoted and re-signed. `maxWalletApprovals` caps how many times (default 5, floored
at 1). Sends and withdrawals never do this.

```ts
import { getPublicKey, serializeUtxo, swapWithChange } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const swapResult = await swapWithChange(
  depositResult.outputUtxos,
  swapAmount,
  outputMint,
  recipientAta,
  minOut,
  {
    connection, programId, relayUrl,
    signMessage: wallet.signMessage!,
    walletPublicKey: getPublicKey(wallet),
    chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk,
    cachedMerkleTree: depositResult.merkleTree,
    swapSlippageBps: 1500,
    maxWalletApprovals: 5,     // swaps only; tell the user they may be asked more than once
  },
  getPublicKey(wallet),        // so the SDK can create the ATA if missing
);

await saveNoteBytes(serializeUtxo(swapResult.outputUtxos[0]));  // change note
await saveSwapRefund(swapResult.refund);                        // timeout-refund secret
```

**Persist `swapResult.outputUtxos[0]` AND `swapResult.refund` before you do anything else, in
either form.** A swap hands back two pieces of the user's own money that exist only in that returned
object. `outputUtxos[0]` is the shielded change note whenever the inputs did not sum to exactly
`swapAmount`, which is the case in both recipes above, and a change note is the one thing NOTHING
recovers: its blinding comes from
`randomFieldElement()` and is written nowhere on chain, so scanning will never bring it back (§5.5).
The `refund` object is the secret that claims the principal back if the swap times out before it
executes (§5.3). Store the change note with `serializeUtxo` (§5.2) and the `refund` object beside
it, the moment the call returns.

Both recipes above pass `chainNoteViewingKeyNk: nk`, so the refund secret is derived from that `nk`
and `discoverSwapRefunds` (§5.5) can rebuild it later from key material alone. That is a backstop,
not a substitute for persisting it.

### 6.7 Compliance history scan + CSV export

```ts
import {
  scanTransactions, toComplianceReport, formatComplianceCsv,
  getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey,
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const nk = getNkFromUtxoPrivateKey(utxoKeypair.privateKey);

const scan = await scanTransactions({
  connection,
  programId,
  viewingKeyNk: nk,
  batchSize: 50,
  walletPublicKey: sender.publicKey.toBase58(),
  onStatus: (s) => console.log("scan:", s),
  onProgress: (done, total) => console.log(`scan progress ${done}/${total}`),
});

console.log("summary", scan.summary);
const report = toComplianceReport(scan);
const csv = formatComplianceCsv(report);
await writeFile("cloak-history.csv", csv, "utf8");
```

Incremental re-scan (only fetch new transactions since the last run):

```ts
import { scanTransactions } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const delta = await scanTransactions({
  connection,
  programId,
  viewingKeyNk: nk,
  untilSignature: scan.lastSignature, // resume cursor
});
```

### 6.8 Viewing-key registration (advanced)

For standard app integrations, keep the SDK-managed registration flow and avoid manual wiring.
Only use direct registration helpers for custom/operator pipelines.

### 6.9 Fee math

```ts
import { calculateFeeBigint, isWithdrawAmountSufficient } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

// SOL, 1.0 SOL gross → fee = 5_000_000 + 3_000_000 = 8_000_000 lamports, net 992_000_000
const solGross = 1_000_000_000n;
const solFee = calculateFeeBigint(solGross);   // 5_000_000 fixed + 0.3 % variable
const solNet = solGross - solFee;
if (!isWithdrawAmountSufficient(solGross)) throw new Error("below the SOL fee floor");

// USDC / USDT, 100.000000 USDC gross. No SDK helper exists for SPL: the fixed component is a
// program constant of 450_000 base units (0.45 token at 6 decimals), charged on-chain from the
// pool's PoolConfig alongside the same 0.3 % variable fee.
// fee = 450_000 + 100_000_000 * 3 / 1000 = 750_000 base units (0.75 USDC), net 99_250_000
const usdcGross = 100_000_000n;
const usdcFee = 450_000n + (usdcGross * 3n) / 1000n;
const usdcNet = usdcGross - usdcFee;
```

The program computes and deducts the fee; these numbers are for display. Never describe them as relay or SDK fees.

### 6.10 Metadata encryption (dual envelope)

```ts
import {
  encryptTransactionMetadata, decryptTransactionMetadata,
  deriveViewingKeyFromUtxoPrivateKey,
} from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const vk = deriveViewingKeyFromUtxoPrivateKey(utxoKeypair.privateKey);
const compliancePublic = await fetchCompliancePublic(); // your own source of truth

const bundle = await encryptTransactionMetadata(
  { txType: "withdraw", commitment, amount: 1000000000, recipient: recipient.publicKey.toBase58(), timestamp: Date.now() },
  vk.publicKey,
  compliancePublic,
  { userPubkey: sender.publicKey },
);

// Later, decrypt for the user:
const decrypted = await decryptTransactionMetadata(bundle.encrypted_user, vk.privateKey);
```

### 6.11 Tree helpers + stale-root preflight (advanced)

Use these helpers for operator-grade diagnostics and custom infrastructure.
They are not required for standard app integrations.

### 6.12 On-chain Merkle proof fallback

```ts
import { computeProofFromChain, getShieldPoolPDAs, NATIVE_SOL_MINT } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

const pdas = getShieldPoolPDAs(programId, NATIVE_SOL_MINT);
const proof = await computeProofFromChain(connection, pdas.merkleTree, leafIndex, true);
// proof: { pathElements, pathIndices, root }
```

Pass the resulting tree into `TransactOptions.cachedMerkleTree` or set `useChainForMerkle: true` to force on-chain reconstruction inside the transact path.

### 6.13 Error handling + retry for stale roots

```ts
import { fullWithdraw, isRootNotFoundError, parseError } from "@cloak.dev/sdk";

for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
  try {
    await fullWithdraw(inputUtxos, recipient, options);
    break;
  } catch (err) {
    if (isRootNotFoundError(err)) {
      const wait = 500 * 2 ** attempt;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait));
      continue;
    }
    const friendly = parseError(err);
    console.error("withdraw failed:", friendly);
    throw err;
  }
}
```

This loop is safe to re-enter only while `inputUtxos` holds one or two notes. With three or more,
the first attempt may already have consolidated some of them on chain, so the same array is no
longer the wallet's live state and a retry spends notes that are gone (§5.2). Guardrail 9 applies:
the SDK transaction paths already retry stale roots, so do not add this loop by default.

---

## 7. Recipe index for common flows

Use section 6 directly as your public, copy-paste integration source. Every recipe there is
written in the Node/server form and carries its own browser form beside it; read the browser block,
do not adapt the Node one by hand.

- Deposit a fresh shielded UTXO: section 6.1.
- Withdraw flows: sections 6.2 (full) and 6.3 (partial/change), including why a full withdrawal is
  storage-free at one or two input notes and not at three or more.
- Private shield-to-shield transfer (private send): section 6.4, including how to make the note
  discoverable by the recipient.
- Fast-send user flow: section 6.5.
- SOL -> SPL swap with shielded change: section 6.6, including the two secrets a swap hands back
  that must be persisted (the change note and `UtxoSwapResult.refund`).
- Recovering a swap refund whose secret was never persisted: `discoverSwapRefunds`, section 5.5.
- Compliance scan and CSV export: section 6.7.
- Viewing-key registration: section 6.8.
- Fee modeling (SOL + SPL): section 6.9.
- Metadata encryption: section 6.10.
- Merkle reliability helpers and fallback proof path: sections 6.11 and 6.12.
- Retry/error strategy for stale roots: section 6.13.

---

## 8. AI generation guardrails (hard rules)

1. Never print/log secrets: spend keys (`skSpend`), viewing keys (`nk`, private bytes), UTXO `privateKey`, `blinding`, note payloads, raw `sign_message` outputs, `cloakKeys`, or relayer auth tokens.
2. Never hand-pack Groth16 public inputs. Let `transact` / `swapUtxo` build the proof and the 264-byte public inputs for you.
3. Never bypass `viewingKeyNk` when calling `scanTransactions`: it cannot return anything without it.
4. Never change `externalAmount` semantics; treat deposit/withdraw/transfer as three distinct modes derived from that field.
5. Never call `transact` with raw `number` amounts. Always `BigInt(...)` at API boundaries.
6. Use SDK defaults for program and circuits in standard integrations. `relayUrl` has no default and must be passed on every flow, as an allowlisted origin. Never generate `relayUrl: ""` together with `enforceViewingKeyRegistration: false` for a send, withdrawal or swap: that pairing is what makes `""` mean direct submission, and it submits under the user's own key, publicly linking the transaction.
7. Prefer `scanTransactions` + `toComplianceReport` for user history UX. Do not re-invent compliance endpoints.
8. For mutating paths in the browser, prefer the wallet adapter (`signTransaction` / `signMessage`). Reserve `depositorKeypair` for Node scripts.
9. Do not add manual stale-root retry loops by default in app scripts; SDK transaction paths already handle these retries.
10. Cache `TransactResult.merkleTree` across operations in the same user session to avoid redundant tree rebuilds.
11. For one-file scripts, accept `<recipientPubkey> <lamports>` in CLI and read signer from `KEYPAIR_PATH`.
12. Do not generate `SENDER_PRIVATE_KEY` or `AMOUNT_SOL` + `parseFloat(...)` patterns.
13. Do not generate `RECIPIENT_ADDRESS` / `SEND_LAMPORTS` env contracts for one-file CLI scripts.
14. For standalone script entrypoints, terminate explicitly with `process.exit(0)` on success and `process.exit(1)` on failure.
15. In BROWSER code, never generate `depositorKeypair`, `Keypair.fromSecretKey`, or a `keypair.json` path for a send/withdraw/swap. A wallet adapter cannot supply one. Generate `signMessage` + `walletPublicKey` from `useWallet()` instead, and guard on `signMessage` being present before offering the action.
16. Never substitute an ephemeral, session or service-held key for the authenticated `sender`. It is the key screened for sanctions; substituting it moves screening off the actual user.
17. Do not hand-roll the request-auth scheme when `submitTransactToRelay` will do. If you do hand-roll it, use `buildRelayAuthPreimage` + `canonicalJson` and read `TRANSACT_AUTH_FIELDS` / `TRANSACT_SWAP_AUTH_FIELDS` from the package rather than retyping them.
18. Never claim an integrator must use a Cloak-operated RPC. Only the submission endpoint is pinned; the `Connection` is entirely the caller's, and any non-loopback RPC works.

---

## 9. Minimal LLM "contract"

When generating Cloak integration code, produce a file-by-file plan that:

1. Declares an explicit `TransactOptions` factory (single source of truth for `connection` and signing; keep `programId` fixed to `CLOAK_PROGRAM_ID`).
2. Exposes `deposit`, `transfer`, `partialWithdraw`, `fullWithdraw`, `swap`, and `scanHistory` primitives using the functions in §5.3, §5.2, §5.5.
3. Persists notes and key material through TWO boundaries, which are not interchangeable:
   - **Notes.** Write `result.outputUtxos` yourself, as `serializeUtxo(...)` bytes (§5.2), in the
     same tick the flow returns. Do NOT route them through a `StorageAdapter`: its methods are typed
     on `CloakNote` (`saveNote`, `loadAllNotes`, `updateNote`, `deleteNote`), a different record
     shape, and the public surface has no converter between the two. Passing `serializeUtxo` bytes to
     `saveNote` does not type-check and does not persist a spendable note.
   - **Key material.** `StorageAdapter.saveKeys` / `loadKeys` (a `CloakKeyPair`) is the ready-made
     home, via `LocalStorageAdapter` or `MemoryStorageAdapter` (§5.13).
   For swaps, `UtxoSwapResult.refund` (§5.3) is a third item and must be persisted too. The full
   storage answer, including how the two boundaries divide, is
   `/sdk/wallet-integration#where-your-notes-live-between-sessions`.
4. Surfaces `onProgress` + `onProofProgress` into the UI layer.
5. Maps relay/on-chain errors through `parseError` + `isRootNotFoundError` into a small typed error union.
6. Includes a CSV export path using `formatComplianceCsv(toComplianceReport(scan))`.
7. Never exports or logs raw secrets.
8. Uses only the exact exported names listed in §5. If a name is not listed here, it is not part of the public SDK contract; treat it as unstable.

---

## 10. Version pinning note

- The `transaction` circuit digests (`EXPECTED_CIRCUIT_HASHES.transaction_*`) are the ceremony pins; `DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_URL` is derived from `TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_VERSION` (`0.2.0`) in `src/config/circuit-release.ts` so URL and digests cannot drift. Never hand-write a circuits URL; use `resolveCircuitsBase()`.
- `DEFAULT_CIRCUITS_URL` is an alias of `DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_CIRCUITS_URL`, kept so older imports keep resolving: same value, same ceremony bundle, never `null` in this build. Either name is safe to read. The pre-ceremony `withdraw_regular` / `withdraw_swap` circuits, and the `CloakSDK` class that loaded them, were removed in 0.2.0; `setCircuitsPath` overrides the base for the ceremony `transaction` bundle only, and the deployed program rejects proofs from any other bundle.
- The SDK currently targets program `zh1eLd6rSphLejbFfJEneUwzHRfMKxgzrgkfwA6qRkW`. Set `programId` explicitly in non-default deployments.
